Temporal focus:

T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — immediate post-fire management decisions, erosion risks
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — multi-decade reforestation horizon, increasing wildfire frequency under climate change

Synopsis:
Following a major wildfire in Serbia's Deliblatska Pescara sand dune reserve, foresters and experts are debating reforestation strategy. The key tension is whether to replant fire-prone species (black pine, black locust) or transition to more resilient broadleaf alternatives. Experts advocate a cautious, phased approach — up to 5 years of observation before large-scale replanting — given that 2023–2025 was Serbia's worst fire period this century. The broader backdrop is an accelerating wildfire trend driven by climate change across Southeast Europe, with parallels drawn to Greece's post-2007 reforestation challenges.
